context:
Preserve reusable generated source data under benchmark_runs/datagen/. Dask
cleanup may remove only Dask-owned spill/runtime directories and loaded
database/output artifacts created for the current verification run; it must
not delete TPC-H source data because read, write, transaction, and related
primitives reuse that source corpus.

Prefer Dask-owned adapter changes first. Use the existing
DataFrameTuningConfiguration memory/spill fields where a user supplied tuning
config exists, and add conservative local defaults only where untuned CLI
Dask currently has no resource envelope. Keep Dask optional: no base install
imports should require Dask.
description:
Dask DataFrame produced repeated exit-137/resource-spike failures in the UAT
sweep, including TPC-H, TPC-DS SF 0.1, read primitives SF 1.0, FlightData, and
TPCHavoc. Dask ClickBench timed out at the 600-second cap. The behavior also
caused transient disk-space dips that recovered after subprocess exit.

anti_patterns.dont: treat exit 137 as a generic benchmark failure

preserves.behavior: Dask remains optional and does not affect base installs.
Resource cleanup must not delete reusable generated benchmark source data.

verifications.command: uv run -- benchbox run --platform dask-df --benchmark tpch --scale 0.01 --phases load,power --non-interactive
verifications.description: Dask local smoke either passes or reports a clear resource-envelope failure.
verifications.expected: completed result or explicit resource-envelope diagnostic, not opaque exit 137

benchbox/platforms/dataframe/pandas_family.py.

W3 should own tests/unit/platforms/dataframe/test_dask_df_coverage.py and,
only if CLI option default assertions change,
tests/unit/platforms/dataframe/test_pandas_family_adapters.py.
work_units.summary: Identify the Dask-owned runtime/config files before editing

work_units.notes:
Query-level reduction isolated the opaque exit-137 reproducer to TPC-H Q10
in the Pandas-family implementation. Predicate pushdown and projection
reduction did not prevent the parent-process kill, while the remaining 21
TPC-H queries passed as a subset. W2 therefore owns a Dask adapter guard
that classifies TPC-H Q10 as a resource-envelope failure before executing
the known parent-killing graph.
